title: Thoreau goes to the woods
hookLine: on 4 July 1845 he moves to Walden Pond to live deliberately and front the essential facts (Walden, chapter 2)

cards: Look back at this week of ordinary saints. Socrates talking on his last day, admitting what he didn't know. Brother Lawrence at the sink.
Julian with the world in her palm. Francis walking out to a wolf. Pascal's coat with its secret page.

None of them were kings. All of them paid attention. The week ends in America, on Independence Day, 1845, with a young man moving his few belongings into a tiny cabin he'd built himself beside a pond.

teach.b: Henry David Thoreau built his cabin on the shore of Walden Pond, near Concord, Massachusetts. One room, a bed, a desk, three chairs. He wrote down exactly what it cost: twenty-eight dollars and twelve and a half cents.
He lived there, as he says, two years and two months.

In his book Walden he explained why: "I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life, and see if I could not learn what it had to teach, and not, when I came to die, discover that I had not lived."
Deliberately. On purpose. Not by default, not by habit, not because everyone else did it that way.
Now the honest part. Walden wasn't the wilderness. The cabin was a short walk from town.
Thoreau went into Concord often, had visitors, and ate meals with family and friends. People point that out as if it spoils the story. It doesn't.
The point was never to vanish; it was to strip life down far enough to see what it's made of. Then he left, saying he had several more lives to live.
So the experiment wasn't the cabin.
It was the question he took there: am I choosing this, or just drifting through it? You don't need a pond to ask it. It fits the next hour just as well.

how: Readers of Walden often take up Thoreau's experiment in small ways: a simpler season, a walk without a phone, or asking of one habit whether it is chosen or just drifted into.

games.why: he builds a one-room cabin at Walden Pond and moves in on July 4, 1845, to live deliberately and see what life is made of.

practice: Choose one small thing you'll do in the next hour anyway, drinking a glass of water, walking to the door, making a call, and picture doing it on purpose, start to finish.
Notice the choice to begin, each part as it happens, and the moment you finish: nothing extra, just awake for the whole thing. When your mind drifts, notice that too, and come back.

wordCard.voice: Thoreau. Two years by a pond, near enough to town, to live deliberately and see what life is made of. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: deliberately. A life chosen on purpose, not just drifted into. That's day ninety-one.
